content.thinking:
It looks like the sandbox path might actually be symlinked to the shared replay-sdk directory, which would explain why the listing matches the pwd contents and includes files from other agents.

Now I'm setting up a new sample file for a "soul scythe" creature, importing the builder, frame, math, path, paint, texture, and glow utilities, then sketching out the metadata and helper functions before starting the main build function with a root joint.

Adding joints and vertebra segments...

Defining grip textures now—using a periodic banding pattern along the handle to alternate between teal highlights and a mottled leather paint for the rest of the surface.

Now I'm working out the gold ring details between grip ends, defining a lathe profile shape for the rings and positioning them just above and below the grip segments so they sit flush with the vertebrae without overlapping. Then I'll move on to the skull geometry pieces.

Shifting to the lower jaw, I'm building it as a frustum box tapering in width and height, tagging it to the jaw bone for rigging, with the blade serving as the tongue and a chin spike for detail. I'm also considering adding a small glowing teal sphere inside the mouth to suggest an inner fire.

Now I'm working out the skeletal structure above the jaw — a collar lathe shape with a dark iron and gold ring finish, a cranium centered around y=1.95 whose base meets the collar, and a ribcage made from six curved sweeps. I'm placing a glowing orb at the shaft's core and adding small bone cup lathes to flesh out the spine between the collar and torso.

Checking that the rib ends buried fine within the collar flare, and that the jaw hinge near the collar top overlaps acceptably. Now positioning the blade root near the upper jaw underside.

The thickened root wedge actually reads as the tongue root, which works fine. Next I'm building the ribbon tail chain and sweep geometry...

Still writing ribbon and gem details...

Checking the spiral rises along +Y so its top sits near y=1.12 with radius 0.12, overlapping slightly with the vertebra spikes around that height, so I'll adjust the starting radius to 0.17 to wrap around the thick spikes cleanly. Then I'm adding glowing octahedron motes scattered along the spiral path for extra detail.

For the ember particles, I'll scatter 22 small octahedron glows around the lower body and another cluster near the top of the blade as floating soul sparks, merging their geometries into a single part since they're all non-indexed octahedrons, which keeps the part count efficient while letting each mote have a randomized size.

Now I'm defining the blade extrusion with its position, thickness, and bevel, then setting up a paint function that samples the top spine's y-coordinate at a given x by interpolating the local outline points, which stay monotonic enough along the blade's length for this approximation to work.

For the color gradient I'm computing depth below the spine and blending through violet into deep teal then bright teal as depth increases, giving a brighter rim near the edge. Then I'm laying out vein curves as polylines offset below the centerline at a couple of depth fractions, using the local normal and width scaling to trace them along the blade.

Still drawing veins and planning glyph placement across the four panels, computing glyph positions relative to the blade width at each panel's center point.

Writing SVG generation code...

Good, the mirroring math checks out. I still need to handle flame, ghost, and rune ring textures, and verify the card texture setup with sink and cross settings looks right, plus glow materials sharing per texture and tint. I'll also make sure palette extras like SOCK are included before writing the full file.
